cases.prompt: A workshop has one cutter and one polisher. The cutter needs 4 minutes per part and the polisher needs 6 minutes per part. A part must be cut before it is polished, buffers are unlimited, and both machines may work at the same time. Starting with an empty workshop, determine the minimum elapsed time to finish 8 parts. Explain the schedule and identify the bottleneck rather than giving only a number.

Five talks—Atlas, Birch, Cobalt, Delta, and Ember—must occupy slots 1 through 5, one per slot. Atlas is earlier than Delta. Birch is immediately after Cobalt. Ember is not first or last. Delta is not adjacent to Ember. List every valid ordering and briefly show how you ruled out the other placements.

Estimate how many liters of drinking water a group of 37 hikers should stage for a 9-hour warm-weather day hike. State explicit assumptions, include a reasonable safety margin, keep arithmetic visible, and separate water intended for drinking from water reserved for cooking or cleaning. This is a planning estimate, not medical advice.

Write a compact Swift 6 actor named ExpiringCache that stores String values by String key with a per-entry ContinuousClock deadline. It needs async-safe set, get, remove, and removeExpired methods. A get after expiration must behave as a miss and delete the stale entry. Explain any Sendable choices and include a short usage example. Prefer standard library and Foundation only.

Explain why a heat pump can deliver more joules of heat to a building than the joules of electrical energy it consumes without violating conservation of energy. Define coefficient of performance, describe where the additional heat originates, and note two conditions that reduce real-world performance.

Compare a B-tree database index with a hash index for equality lookup, ordered range scans, write amplification, and locality. Then give one concrete query pattern for which each index is the better default. Avoid product-specific claims.

A screening test has 96% sensitivity and 92% specificity. In a population where 3% of people have the condition, compute the probability that a randomly selected person who tests positive actually has it. Show the calculation using an imagined cohort of 10,000 people and explain why the result differs from 96%.

Read the synthetic expedition log and answer the questions at the end. Preserve exact identifiers and distinguish observations from inferences.

Day 1: Team Juniper established Base LARK-17 beside the western moraine. The weather station reported 1008 hPa and light wind. Crate K2 held sampling bags; crate M4 held spare batteries. No instruments were deployed.

Day 2: Transect A began at marker A-00. Samples A-01 through A-05 were dry gravel. At A-06, technician Nia noted a narrow band of dark silt but did not collect it because the bag seal was damaged. The team returned to base before rain.

Day 3: Rain delayed departure until 11:20. Crate M4 was opened and battery pack BP-9 was installed in spectrometer SABLE. At marker A-06, Nia collected replacement sample A-06R from the dark silt band. SABLE displayed calibration warning W3, so the reading was marked provisional: iron index 0.42.

Day 4: Engineer Omar found dust on SABLE's reference tile, cleaned it with distilled water, and ran standards ST-LOW and ST-HIGH. Both fell within tolerance. A second reading of A-06R produced iron index 0.61. The field notebook explicitly says the Day 3 value should not be used for comparison. Team Juniper then extended Transect A to A-11; no other dark silt was seen.

Day 5: Team Kestrel arrived from the eastern route with sealed sample E-14, described as pale clay from Ridge RAVEN. Their handheld instrument, FINCH, reported iron index 0.18. Because FINCH and SABLE use different reference curves, Omar wrote that the two indices are not directly comparable without lab normalization.

Day 6: Wind prevented ridge work. Nia inventoried supplies: 18 intact sampling bags in K2, 6 damaged seals quarantined in Q1, and three charged packs in M4. A radio summary accidentally called E-14 a western-moraine sample; the signed notebook retained the eastern Ridge RAVEN origin.

Day 7: The team packed out. Chain-of-custody forms list A-06R as collected by Nia on Day 3 at western marker A-06, and E-14 as transferred by Team Kestrel on Day 5 from eastern Ridge RAVEN. Both samples were delivered unopened to Lab Cedar.

Questions: (1) Which iron-index value for A-06R is suitable for later comparison, and why? (2) What is the authoritative origin of E-14? (3) Name the instrument and battery pack used for A-06R. (4) State one comparison the log does not justify.

You are given an original synthetic service incident timeline. Produce a concise root-cause summary, contributing factors, and three follow-up actions. Do not blame the database unless the evidence supports it.

09:02 UTC — Release R41 begins on two of eight API workers. Health checks pass.
09:07 — p95 latency rises from 180 ms to 410 ms only on R41 workers. Error rate is unchanged.
09:10 — Autoscaling adds two workers, both R41. Queue depth falls briefly, then rises again.
09:13 — Metrics show CPU at 38%, memory at 51%, database query time steady at 24 ms, and outbound object-store calls rising from 2 to 19 per request.
09:16 — An engineer observes that requests containing six or more attachments are slow; requests without attachments remain near baseline.
09:19 — Feature flag attach_manifest_v2 is disabled. New R41 workers stop making repeated object-store metadata calls, but the original four R41 workers continue doing so.
09:23 — Investigation finds the flag value was copied into a process-local singleton at startup rather than read per request. The runbook had described the flag as dynamically reversible.
09:27 — The four affected R41 workers are drained and restarted. Latency returns to 185 ms and queue depth clears.
09:34 — Code review identifies an inner loop that fetches the complete attachment manifest once for every attachment, even though the manifest is identical for the request. R40 fetched it once outside the loop.
09:41 — No data loss or incorrect responses are found. Object-store throttling never occurred. The database stayed within normal load throughout.

Return exactly one valid JSON object and no Markdown. Use keys `normalized`, `word_count`, `has_question`, and `tags`. Normalize the sentence by trimming outer whitespace and collapsing internal runs of whitespace to one space. Count words by whitespace after normalization. `tags` must be a sorted array containing `greeting` if the sentence greets someone and `planning` if it asks about a future plan.

Sentence: `   Hello   Mira,   are we hiking   tomorrow?   `

Rewrite the note below as a calm, direct status update of 70 to 100 words. Keep all concrete facts, remove speculation and emotional language, and end with one explicit next step.

Note: We had another awful sync failure at 14:05. Seven records are delayed, not lost. The retry worker is running and has already recovered four. The remaining three reference an old schema version. Priya is checking the migration logs. Customers can still create and read current records. We think everything will probably be fine, but nobody knows yet.
